literal: Energy possession (is) possession; wealth possession without staying having departed will leave.
translation: The possession of inner energy is true possession. The possession of material wealth will not endure and will slip away.
modern: ஊக்கத்தை உடையவராக இருப்பதே உண்மையான உடைமையாகும். பொருட்செல்வம் நிலைத்து நிற்காமல் ஒருவரை விட்டு நீங்கிப் போய்விடும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts inner drive with external wealth. The word 'uḷḷam' generally means the mind, but in the context of this chapter, it specifically refers to the mind's energy or motivation. The poet states that possessing this inner energy is the only real wealth a person can have. Material wealth ('poruḷ'), on the other hand, is temporary; it does not stay fixed and will eventually disappear. Therefore, true security lies in one's own enduring motivation rather than in fleeting possessions.
